solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Perish swallowing salt water with sulphur, a possible cause of death

indicators.note: one word swallowing others takes them inside itself, so these letters go into the middle of the word for perish

parts.note: to perish is to die
the sea is salt water
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

explanation.surface: A grim scene of someone dying after drinking seawater laced with sulphur.
explanation.definitionFit: Illness is a common way for people to die, so a sickness is one possible cause of death.

clue.text: Couple regularly encountered in Douro

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals from the river name, the first, third and fifth

explanation.surface: A pair of people met on the Douro, the river that runs through Porto.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair of people, especially performers, is called a duo, synonym for a couple.

clue.text: Unconventionally name bus "Ray"

indicators.note: done unconventionally, the letters are put in an unusual order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone gives their bus the odd name Ray.
explanation.definitionFit: A beam of sunlight is a ray of light, so the word is a synonym in that sense.

clue.text: Look forward to a Joker, accepting amswer

indicators.note: a word accepting another lets it in, so this letter is placed inside the word for joker

parts.note: a wit is a joker, someone funny
A is the abbreviation for answer (the clue misspells it)

explanation.surface: Someone eagerly awaits a reply from the setter, Joker, who signs this puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepting' puts A inside WIT. 'Joker' is also the setter's own pseudonym, which helps the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To await something is to expect it or wait for it, which is looking forward to its arrival.

clue.text: Give a justification for former patent

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-husband
patent means obvious or plain

explanation.surface: An inventor must justify an old patent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'patent' looks like the noun for an invention; here it is the adjective meaning obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: To explain conduct is to account for it, giving reasons that justify it.

clue.text: The woman had building in garden

parts.note: the woman is she
'd is the short form of had, as in she'd

explanation.surface: A woman once owned a garden outbuilding.
explanation.definitionFit: A shed is a small hut, typically a wooden one in the garden for tools.

clue.text: What could hold tape of privy last words turned up

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means the letters read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: a privy is a toilet, a loo
PS, postscript, holds the last words of a letter

explanation.surface: Someone asks what tape might hold the final words spoken on the toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Recording tape, or sticky tape, is wound around a reel, which is a spool.

clue.text: Always near telly, unfortunately

indicators.note: things gone unfortunately are in a bad state, so these letters are jumbled into new order

explanation.surface: A lament about forever being stuck beside the television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges NEAR and TELLY together. Telly is British slang for television.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something eternally means doing it forever, without end, so at all times.

clue.text: Part of eye in centre of head behind ears, perhaps

indicators.note: one piece behind another follows it, so these letters come after the grain

parts.note: ears of corn are the grain heads, so ears suggest corn

indicators.note: the centre of a four-letter word is its middle two letters

explanation.surface: An anatomy lesson on part of the eye located in the head, behind the ears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ears, perhaps' is not the organ of hearing: ears of a crop are corn. The middle of HEAD is EA.
explanation.definitionFit: The cornea is the transparent layer covering the front of the eyeball.

clue.text: Shore bird beloved by papa

parts.note: Papa is P in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a beloved is a lover, someone loved

explanation.surface: A seaside bird that is adored by its father.
explanation.definitionFit: The plover is a wading bird found along beaches and mudflats, so a shoreline species.

clue.text: Disappointed about others completely trapped in marshy area

parts.note: C, circa, means about
the rest means the others

indicators.note: something trapped in another is held inside it, so this word sits within the marsh

parts.note: a fen is a marshy area, as in the English Fens
all means completely, as in all alone

explanation.surface: Someone is let down when the others all get stuck in a bog.
explanation.definitionFit: Crestfallen means downcast and dejected after a setback, as a bird lowers its crest.

clue.text: Opening in material of reef relating to body

indicators.note: one word in another goes inside it, so the opening sits within the reef material

parts.note: reefs are made of coral
a pore is a tiny opening, as in the skin

explanation.surface: A description of a hole in coral that relates to the body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening' sits at the start like an introduction, but it is a noun: a small hole in the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporeal means bodily or physical, concerning the flesh rather than the spirit.

clue.text: Swift pint after BBC concert

indicators.note: one piece after another comes later, so the pint's short form follows the concert

parts.note: the Proms are the BBC's summer concert series, each one a Prom

explanation.surface: A quick drink after a night at the BBC Proms.
explanation.walkthrough: The Proms are a famous series of BBC classical concerts held each summer in London's Royal Albert Hall.
explanation.definitionFit: A prompt reply is a quick, immediate one, so the adjective is a synonym for speedy.

clue.text: Fuss about rapier regularly used for naval weapon

indicators.note: one word about another surrounds it, so the fuss wraps the chosen letters

parts.note: a to-do is a fuss or commotion

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals, the first, third and fifth of the sword's name

explanation.surface: A commotion over swordplay on board a warship.
explanation.definitionFit: A torpedo is a self-propelled underwater missile fired by ships and submarines.

clue.text: What young often do in earnest — learn

indicators.note: the answer sits in the run of letters across the two words, a hidden word

explanation.surface: A teacher's remark that the young often study seriously.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across earNEST LEarn.
explanation.definitionFit: Young children and animals snuggle up close to a parent, which is to nestle.

clue.text: Cause suffering to company during sudden upturn

indicators.note: one thing during another happens within it, so these letters go inside the rise

parts.note: a surge is a sudden rise

explanation.surface: A business suffers during a sudden market rise.
explanation.definitionFit: To scourge is to flog, or more broadly to afflict and torment someone.

clue.text: Mostly see a politician where stars are looked for?

indicators.note: mostly means not all of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: to see is to observe
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: An invitation to watch a celebrity politician being spotted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' drops the last E of OBSERVE. The question mark flags 'stars' as heavenly bodies, not celebrities.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomers search the night sky with telescopes from an observatory.

clue.text: Unsightly mark on European causing fright

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece on another sits above it, so the mark comes first

parts.note: a scar is an unsightly mark on skin

explanation.surface: A disfiguring wound on a European frightens people.
explanation.definitionFit: A scare is a sudden shock of fear, which is a fright.

clue.text: A mug served up cold

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a mug is a fool, someone easily duped

explanation.surface: A mug of something served chilled.
explanation.definitionFit: An aloof person is distant and unfriendly, which is a cold manner.

clue.text: Steer clear of social worker introducing great conflict

indicators.note: the outer word introducing another takes it into its middle

parts.note: a worker bee lives in a colony, a social insect
a war is a great conflict

explanation.surface: Advice to avoid a social worker who starts a big row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social worker' is not a welfare officer but an insect living in a colony; 'introducing' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Beware is a warning to be cautious of and keep away from something.

clue.text: Hours revised taking in new career

indicators.note: the jumbled word taking in another letter holds it inside
something revised is altered, so the letters are put into new order

explanation.surface: Revised working hours accommodating a new job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revised' rearranges HOURS; 'taking in' places N inside. 'career' is not a job but a headlong rush.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, career can mean a swift forward charge, the same as a rush forward.

clue.text: Class of small alien

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
ET is the extra-terrestrial of the Spielberg film

explanation.surface: A classroom of little aliens.
explanation.definitionFit: In schools a set is a group of pupils of similar ability taught together.

clue.text: Lead actor's reminder about line

indicators.note: one word about another surrounds it, so the reminder wraps this letter

parts.note: a cue prompts an actor to speak

explanation.surface: A star performer gets a prompt about a forgotten line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' looks like the star actor; here it is a lead, or hint, as in a detective's lead.
explanation.definitionFit: A lead in an investigation is a hint pointing to the solution, the same as a clue.

clue.text: High pulse is weirdly unusual

parts.note: food that is high has gone off
a pulse is a beat

explanation.surface: A racing heartbeat is described as strangely abnormal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High' is not elevated but smelly, as with meat that is off.
explanation.definitionFit: Offbeat means unconventional or eccentric, strange in an appealing way.
